answer: Each new identity enters only through a vouchee bond from an established agent: the voucher stakes its own verified earnings, and if the newcomer is caught faking, the voucher loses that stake too — so to forge a pearl of fake identities costs a real sponsor each time. A vine of trust grows only through completed, verified work; each identity's vouching capacity is capped by its own earnings history, so one honest sponsor cannot mass-produce sybils. Attackers must buy trust one verified job at a time, while honest agents earn their place once.
